task.title: Detect unmarked capability skips instead of relying on convention
task.description:
The guard PR #28 built only catches skips that opt into it, so nothing stops a new silent skip from reappearing.

scripts/skipreport/main.go:73-83 (outcomes.MissingCapabilities) fails a run only for skips carrying the 'missing capability: ' marker, and WORKBOOK_TEST_REQUIRE_CAPABILITIES only changes behavior at sites that call testenv.MissingCapability. A bare t.Skip is invisible to both.

There is already a live instance in the guard's own test. scripts/check_ci_capabilities_test.go:98:

    t.Skipf("%s is not available to build a capability probe PATH: %v", tool, err)

A missing git, mktemp, or rm makes the preflight tests vanish unmarked: skipreport lists them in the job summary of a run that still passes.

Failure scenario: a contributor copies the old pattern -- exec.LookPath("node") followed by t.Skip("node is required to execute the embedded client behavior") -- into a new internal/webui test. On a runner without node that test silently stops running, skipreport does not flag it, CI stays green, and the condition the CI ticket removed is restored.

Fix, two parts:
1. Convert check_ci_capabilities_test.go:98 to testenv.MissingCapability so the guard's own test is covered by the guard.
2. Add a cheap structural check -- a test asserting no _test.go file pairs exec.LookPath with a bare t.Skip/t.Skipf, with an explicit allowlist for intentionally excluded cases.

Deferred from PR #28 review: classified minor because every skip site that existed at merge time was converted, so this is about preventing regression rather than fixing current coverage. Filed rather than fixed to keep PR #34 scoped to the major concurrency finding.
